what: The one held-out evaluation of the trained segmenters (dacl10k v1, v2a, v2b, v2c) and the classical engine, each at its profile (drishyam.agent.PROFILES, unchanged) and charged the cost table the dev comparison charged it, each held-out set scored once per model. Nothing was tuned on these numbers. v2c was scored later than the others, after its own dev calibration; the others' runs were not repeated. v1-policy2, v1 with the configuration its dev rule chose, was scored once more, later, beside v1 (whose runs were not repeated): see the v1-policy2 block.
criterion: The dev comparison's criterion (results/dev/model_choice_dev.json), unchanged, on the held-out counterparts of its splits: recall at the 30 % cap on CODEBRIM eval200 (for dev100) and synth200 (for synth_dev), and false alarms at the 30 % cap on the clean set synth_clean (for the clean dev split). A is better than B on a set when the paired 95 % bootstrap CI of A's recall ratio to B lies wholly above 1, worse when wholly below; A harms against B on the clean set when the CI of its boxes-per-photo difference or of its difference in the share of photos with any box lies wholly above 0. The dev choice of v1 rested on v1 being the only model with no measurable loss against any other (where_each_loses), so that is what this checks.

dev_choice.statement: Held-out confirms the dev choice: v1 is again the only model with no measurable loss against any other on CODEBRIM eval200, synth200 or the clean set.

cost_note: Each model is charged its own table, timed on this Mac (x86, 1 cv2 thread per worker): v2b results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2b/micro.json (2026-10-19T19:28Z, 1-min load 10.64 at start, 14.52 at end), v2a results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json (2026-10-19T16:27Z, 1-min load 7.93 at start, 7.81 at end), v1 results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json (2026-10-19T16:31Z, 1-min load 8.0 at start, 7.39 at end), the classical engine results/local-macos-x86/micro.json (2026-10-17T20:19Z, 1-min load 23.82 at start, none recorded at end). One look at 4000x3000 (warp, quality and segment:accurate, p50) costs 1326.8 ms on v2b's table, 526.5 on v2a's, 568.1 on v1's and 108.0 on the classical engine's. v2a re-timed in v2b's window (runs/v2a/micro/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json, load 14.08 to 11.22) costs 1304.5: per look v2b costs 0.87 to 1.04 times v2a in one window across the three timed sizes, against 2.10 to 2.52 between their own tables, so the ms gap between v2b and v2a below is the machine load at timing, not the model. v1 and v2a were timed in one window (0.97 to 1.10 per look). The classical table's high load overstates its ms, so the ONNX models' ratios to it understate their extra cost at equal load. v2c is charged its own table too, results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2c/micro.json (2026-10-20T10:48Z, 1-min load 9.51 at start, 7.02 at end), where one look at 4000x3000 costs 744.9 ms. v2a re-timed in v2c's window (runs/v2c/micro/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json, load 7.02 to 7.36) costs 749.4: per look v2c costs 0.99 times v2a at each of the three timed sizes in one window (the same encoder), against 1.22 to 1.41 between their own tables, so the ms gap between v2c and v2a (and v1, timed in v2a's window) below is the machine load at timing, not the model.

prior_exposure: v1 had been scored on two of these sets before, once each, on 2026-10-18 and never published: CODEBRIM eval200 (run started 14:07Z) and synth200 (00:52Z), with the agent of that day, before its dev profile, on its first cost table (results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k). The runs are in the main checkout's ignored runs/model-eval/. So for v1 these are second scorings; v2a and v2b had never been scored on any held-out set (no other run under runs/ or a worktree carries these sets' sha256s with an ONNX segmenter). Nor had v2c before its run here: its only earlier jobs were the install's smoke jobs on three of the demo's bridge photos (the main checkout's runs/model-smoke/), and no run folder under runs/ or a worktree names it.

v1-policy2.prior_exposure: v1-policy2 is v1 with the configuration results/dev/policy2_sweep.json chose on the dev splits (g_s60: first looks on the tiling grid, a confirm look at the same level for a critical mask under confidence 0.6, which otherwise goes to a person as needs-a-look, critical classes weighted x2 in the look score, overlapping critical findings of one class merged) and the zero-candidate fallback on. It is v1's third read of CODEBRIM eval200 and synth200 and its second of the clean set: v1 was scored on CODEBRIM eval200 and synth200 on 2026-10-18 (unpublished, see prior_exposure) and on all three in its published run here. A held-out run of v1 with the fallback alone was started on 2026-10-21 in another worktree and stopped; its output was never read or used. This configuration was chosen on dev after those reads, by a rule stated before its dev run, and nothing was changed after this read.

dev_rule_on_held_out.note: results/dev/policy2_sweep.json's clauses (evals.policy2.clauses, unchanged) on the held-out counterparts of its splits (synth200 for synth_dev, CODEBRIM eval200 for dev100, the clean set for the clean dev split), against v1 at the 30 % cap.
